label: ercot128 unit grain coal
definition: ERCOT-128 Phase 2, REGISTERED AS A REJECTED PROBE — the ercot115 keeper recipe with a single delta, ercot_coal_min_config_floor armed in its availability-SCALED form (a per-tranche constant left to the generic clip to pmax x availability). It passed every absolute gate — G1 19/21 tying the outgoing keeper, C1 coal -0.955/-0.102/-1.678 TWh, C1 all 16/16 free 12/12, coal forced share 2.94/2.92/2.30 % inside the 30 % cap, D-4 off-window 0.0 % — and was REJECTED anyway, because it failed its own pre-registered STRUCTURAL claim: physically-impossible online plant-hours (plant online but below its own min_u MinLoad_u) went 14,582 -> 14,886 / 13,020 -> 13,051 / 9,558 -> 9,561, i.e. it removed essentially none of the impossible loadings it exists to remove while forcing 1.4-1.7 TWh/yr. Root cause: a minimum online configuration does not shrink when units go out, so scaling it by availability puts the applied floor below the physical minimum exactly where the defect lives. Superseded by 2026-07-28-ercot129-conditional-coal-min, which fixes the expression (availability-CONDITIONAL) and is the current ERCOT keeper; the two runs share the same flag, artifact, mechanism id and cache key, so they are a true A/B on one expression — and the evidence that the gates alone would have promoted the wrong build. Determination NOT-YET. Full forensics: docs/DIAGNOSIS-ercot128-coal-unit-grain-2026-07-28.md §§P1-P5.
